name: Air Command
tagline: A sip-and-puff sensor that works as a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse for people with limited mobility.
problem: Computer access is hard for people with limited mobility.
solution: An air-pressure sensor on a single-board computer feeds a state machine that classifies sips and puffs and emulates a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.
demo_moment: Team-described: type and click on a computer by sipping and puffing.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won “[MLH] Best Use of Snowflake API” among 217 submissions.
Emulates a standard input device, so it works with any computer.

lessons: Pretending to be a standard device removes every integration problem.
